\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Timed universal nondeterministic simulation]
\lean{Turing.exists_timed_universal_NDTM}
\label{Turing.exists_timed_universal_NDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.pairEncode}
For every effective code for finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machines with two
work tapes, there is a finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machine $U_N$ such that,
for each Boolean string $\alpha$, some natural number $C$ works for every Boolean string
$x$ and every natural number $t$. On input
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, every choice sequence of length
exactly $C(t+1)$ causes $U_N$ to halt. Moreover, $U_N$ has an accepting computation of
exactly that length if and only if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ has an accepting
computation on $x$ using exactly $t$ nondeterministic choices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deciding bounded nondeterministic acceptance]
\lean{Turing.exists_ndAcceptsWithin_decider}
\label{Turing.exists_ndAcceptsWithin_decider}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.pairEncode}
For every effective coding scheme $c$ for nondeterministic two-work-tape machines over
the binary alphabet, there exists a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine $B$ such that,
for every binary code string $\alpha$, there is a natural-number constant $C$ with the
following property. For every binary input $x$ and every natural number $t$, if the
machine decoded from $\alpha$ accepts $x$ along some choice string of length exactly
$t$, then $B$ computes output $[1]$ on the paired encoding of the binary representation
of $t$, $\alpha$, and $x$ in exactly $C\,2^{C(t+1)}$ steps; if it does not accept in
this sense, then $B$ computes output $[0]$ on that same input in exactly $C\,2^{C(t+1)}$
steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coding a Finite Nondeterministic Machine]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.exists_codeNDTM_accepts_linear}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.exists_codeNDTM_accepts_linear}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM, Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin}
For every finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet,
there are a two-work-tape binary-choice machine $M$ with states indexed by an initial
segment of the natural numbers and a natural number $C$ such that, for every binary
input $x$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, if $N$ accepts $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $M$
accepts $x$ in exactly $C(t+1)$ steps; conversely, if $M$ accepts $x$ in exactly $t$
steps, then $N$ accepts $x$ in some number of steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nondeterministic Time Hierarchy]
\lean{Complexity.ntime_hierarchy}
\label{Complexity.ntime_hierarchy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be time-constructible functions: each $T\in\{f,g\}$
satisfies $n\le T(n)$ for every $n$, and some positive constant $c$ and finite
deterministic Turing machine compute the binary expansion of $T(|x|)$ on every input $x$
within $c(T(|x|)+1)$ steps. Suppose that for every natural number $A$ there is an $N$
such that, for all $n\ge N$, $A\bigl(f(n+1)+f(n)+n+1\bigr)\le g(n)$. Then
$\mathrm{NTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{NTIME}(n\mapsto g(n)+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive-Bound Nondeterministic Time Hierarchy]
\lean{Complexity.ntime_hierarchy_of_pos}
\label{Complexity.ntime_hierarchy_of_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be time-constructible functions: each $T\in\{f,g\}$
satisfies $n\le T(n)$ for every $n$, and some positive constant $c$ and finite
deterministic Turing machine compute the binary expansion of $T(|x|)$ on every input $x$
within $c(T(|x|)+1)$ steps. Suppose $g(n)>0$ for every $n$, and for every natural number
$A$ there is an $N$ such that, for all $n\ge N$, $A\bigl(f(n+1)+f(n)+n+1\bigr)\le g(n)$.
Then $\mathrm{NTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{NTIME}(g)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict separation of linear and quadratic time]
\lean{Complexity.NTIME_linear_ssubset_square}
\label{Complexity.NTIME_linear_ssubset_square}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME}
Among languages of binary strings, every language decidable nondeterministically within
time proportional to the input length plus one is decidable nondeterministically within
time proportional to the square of the input length plus one; moreover, some language in
the latter class is not in the former.
\end{theorem}
